subject: Retro billing apportionment & VAT ID validation for Q4 invoice
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <finance@greenwave-analytics.com>

Cc: Robert Kim <robert.kim@greenwave-uk.co.uk>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: split invoice & VAT treatment (retro-apportionment)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Our accounting team spotted that the entity handover that occurred on Nov 18 means our Q4 usage crosses a place-of-supply boundary (EU entity -> UK entity). We need Redwood to:

- Reissue the Nov 1–30 invoice split into two lines (EU entity share + UK entity share) with clear tax treatment per line (reverse-charge where applicable for intra-EU; UK VAT treatment post-brexit).
- Apply a retro apportionment: 55% EU / 45% UK for November usage (driven by seat ownership timeline).
- Validate both VAT registrations and include the validated VAT numbers on the invoice for our auditors.

I've attached the original invoice and our VAT certificate snapshot. Can you confirm whether Redwood will reissue the invoice or if you prefer we self-bill? We need the reissued documents by COB Dec 7 to close the month.

Attachments: invoice_2026Q4_original.pdf (pdf), greenwave_vat_cert_2026.png (image)

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Finance — Greenwave Analytics
finance@greenwave-analytics.com
+44 20 7946 0123

Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: split invoice & VAT treatment (retro-apportionment)

Hi Marta — thanks for the details and the attachments. We can reissue the invoice from our side and include the validated VAT numbers on the document. Next steps from Redwood:

1) Billing ops (cc'd Marcus) will prepare a split/reissued invoice with two lines and the requested apportionment percentages.
2) Finance (cc'd Laura) will confirm tax treatment per line (reverse-charge flags for applicable EU to EU B2B flows and UK VAT classification for post-Nov 18 usage).
3) Tax team will run the two VAT numbers through VIES (EU) and gov.uk validation for the UK one and will embed validation results in the reissued PDF.

Two asks for you so we can proceed immediately:
- Please confirm the exact legal names and VAT numbers for the EU entity and the UK entity (copy/paste is safest).
- Confirm whether you want us to include a short note on the invoice referencing the entity change (e.g., “Usage apportioned per intercompany handover on 2026-11-18”).

I'll chase Marcus for a turnaround estimate — aiming for a reissue by Tue COB (Dec 7) if we get the VAT numbers today.

Best,
— Soojin

Subject: Fwd: Request: split invoice & VAT treatment (retro-apportionment)

Marcus / Laura — forwarding Greenwave request. TL;DR: they need the Nov invoice reissued with 55% LU / 45% UK apportionment and the VAT numbers validated and recorded on the invoice. Deadlines: customer needs documents by COB Tue Dec 7.

Tax specifics to include on the reissue (please implement):
- Line 1 (EU): amount = original_amount * 0.55; VAT handling = B2B reverse-charge; include VIES validation result (timestamped).
- Line 2 (UK): amount = original_amount * 0.45; VAT handling = UK VAT not charged by Redwood (customer to self-account) OR if required by finance, show 0% VAT with note referencing customer UK VAT registration and validation outcome.
- Invoice footer: "Usage apportioned per intercompany handover on 2026-11-18. See HubSpot ticket for supporting docs."

Validation steps: please run both numbers via VIES and gov.uk API; capture validation screenshots and embed as an annex to the PDF (or include as separate attachment). If VIES returns any error for LU number, escalate to tax@redwoodinference.com and mark invoice as "pending validation"; do not finalize until we have a clean response.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/ticket/98765 (customer ticket with timeline)
Attachments to append to reissued PDF: greenwave_vat_cert_2026.png (provided by customer)

Marcus — can you confirm ETA and whether we need a credit note for the original invoice? If a credit is required, include a small explanatory credit referencing the original invoice id.

Thanks,
Soojin
